label: late copy-phase steps re-inputting p/j/r/2/h-like tokens
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during the original tokens or on <DEL>), and essentially never before recall_idx 2. The firing rate rises with absolute step t and with recall position: about 1% at t<=8, 23-34% at t>=12, so long sequences (L=8-9) carry most of the mass. Within those steps it prefers particular fed-back input tokens: p is strongest (25% rate, 23% of mass, and the top examples are almost all on p), then j, r, 2 and h (about 13-17%), then 3, u, g, k and n. It is weak on s and v. Activations often come in runs over consecutive copy steps that build up toward a p. The output token and next_out matter much less. The predicate (copy phase, recall_idx>=3, t>=10, input in that 10-token set) gets dev F1 0.59 with mass recall 0.83. Many steps that fit the predicate stay inactive, and some activations fall on tokens outside the set, so the token preference is graded and depends on context rather than being a clean set.
